name: Saltline
description: A neural-feed film in which the viewer inhabits Mara Vasquez-Osei, a biological compliance auditor who discovers that a Tier 3 residential water system has been used for a decade to deliver low-dose neurochemical agents that suppress political organizing behavior. The film is technically sophisticated — the neural experience of slow cognitive dulling, of reaching for a thought that keeps sliding away, is rendered with harrowing precision — and was made by a team of former Vantablack engineers who fled to unincorporated territory. It has never been screened on licensed infrastructure.
cultural_impact: Saltline triggered the largest single-month spike in private water filtration purchases in M88 history and remains a live political controversy, with Tier 3 civic groups demanding independent water testing.
story_hooks: The neural-capture data for the cognitive dulling sequence required a real subject — someone actually experienced it, and finding that person is the key to proving the film's central claim.
MAU's criminal complaint names a distribution node in the Shelf that doesn't exist — someone inside MAU is using the complaint as a message.
A licensed neural-health clinic has been quietly treating patients whose BCI logs show anomalous suppression patterns consistent with what Saltline depicts.
